stem: Alcohols \((\mathrm{R-OH})\), phenols \((\mathrm{Ar-OH})\) and carboxylic acids \((\mathrm{R-COOH})\) can undergo ionization of \(\mathrm{O-H}\) bond to give away proton \(\mathrm{H^{\oplus}}\); yet they have different \(\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a}\) values, which are 16, 10 and 4.5 respectively. Explain
solution:
\(\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a}\) value is indicative of acid strength. Lower the \(\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a}\) value stronger the acid. Alcohols, phenols and carboxylic acids, all involve ionization of an \(\mathrm{O-H}\) bond. But their different \(\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a}\) values indicate that their acid strength are different. This is because the resulting conjugate bases are stabilized to different extent.

| Acid (HA) | Conjugate base \((\mathrm{A^{\ominus}})\) | Electronic effect | Stabilization/destabilization |
|---|---|---|---|
| \(\mathrm{R-O-H}\) | \(\mathrm{R \rightarrow O^{\ominus}}\) | \(+\mathrm{I}\) effect of R group | destabilization of conjugate base |
| \(\mathrm{Ar-O-H}\) | \(\mathrm{Ar-O^{\ominus}}\) | \(-\mathrm{R}\) effect or Ar group | stabilization of conjugate base is moderate because all the resonance structures are not equivalent to each other |
| \(\mathrm{R-C(=O)-O-H}\) | \(\mathrm{R-C(=O)-O^{\ominus}}\) | \(-\mathrm{R}\) effect of \(\mathrm{C=O}\) group | stabilization is good because all the resonance structures are equivalent to each other |

As the conjugate base of carboxylic acid is best stabilized, among the three, carboxylic acids are strongest and have the lowest \(\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a}\) value. As conjugate base of alcohols is destabilized, alcohols are weakest acids and have highest \(\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a}\) value. As conjugate base of phenols is moderately stabilized phenols are moderately acidic and have intermediate \(\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a}\) value.
